clue.text: Classified as donkey or small bear?

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
Ted, short for teddy, is a small toy bear

explanation.surface: A zoologist wonders whether to file an animal as a donkey or a little bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of a teddy as a small bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Things sorted into classes or kinds have been grouped, a synonym for being sorted.

clue.text: Summer-time opening of amusements in Georgian town

parts.note: August is a month of summer in the northern hemisphere

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so take the start of amusements

explanation.surface: Holiday entertainments open for the summer season in a town in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' points to the US state, not the former Soviet republic or the 18th-century British era.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is a city in the US state of Georgia, famous for its golf course.

clue.text: Arise and cast off for flight

indicators.note: off here means out of order or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stands up and sets off on a journey by air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges ARISE plus CAST. 'flight' looks like air travel, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors, which is what this structure is.

clue.text: Doubled to get finished

explanation.surface: Someone doubled up in order to complete something.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor who has doubled a cape has sailed around it; to have finished something off is to have completed it.

clue.text: Skilful execution seen in single figure mounted on board

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means climbing upwards, so the whole construction is read bottom to top
seen in places one word inside the other

parts.note: nine is a number of a single digit
art is skill in carrying something out

explanation.surface: An artistic display shows a lone figure perched on a plank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' makes the container and 'mounted' reverses it all, as a down entry is read upwards; the newspaper's 'board' was misread as 'beard'.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a train is to get on it, the sense of this railway verb.

clue.text: About to plant fruit-stone? Excellent

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: to pot is to plant in a container
a pit is the stone of a fruit such as a cherry

explanation.surface: A gardener is on the point of sowing a fruit stone and calls it splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the point of', but it reverses POTPIT. 'Excellent' after the question mark is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal word for first-rate or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Can rage within, and finally change colour

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a tin is a can
anger is rage

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word change

explanation.surface: Someone bottles up their fury until at last their face changes hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerine is an orange shade named after the small citrus fruit.

clue.text: Hypocritical villain in dugout

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious, so falsely righteous
a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A two-faced scoundrel hides out in a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dugout' suggests a trench or a sports shelter; here it is a canoe hollowed from a log.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a canoe made by hollowing out a tree trunk.

clue.text: Turned to view old boy's literary effort

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil
verse is a piece of poetic writing

explanation.surface: A former pupil looks over a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse of a coin or medal is the side facing the observer, the main face.

clue.text: Mark for steady progress, university held

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one letter goes within the longer word

parts.note: gradation is progress by steady stages

explanation.surface: A student's steady improvement earns a grade while at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is a noun: a line on a measuring vessel, not a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduations are the scale lines on a measuring jug or thermometer.

clue.text: Wander over, then run to the front

indicators.note: to the front says one letter is shifted to the start of the word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone strolls across and then dashes forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to roam about without a fixed route.

clue.text: Composer who created conflict and glared horribly

parts.note: sired means fathered or brought into being
war is conflict

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters of glared are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician is accused of starting a war and scowling fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar was an English composer, knighted, famous for the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: The devil is an evil fellow

parts.note: bad means evil
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Satan is simply described as a wicked man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' looks like any man, but it is a college fellow, a don.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaddon is a name for the destroying angel of the Book of Revelation, identified with Satan.

clue.text: How to feed pet without delay?

explanation.surface: A question about the right way to feed a pet promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet may take food straight from your palm; something dismissed instantly is rejected immediately, with no thought.

clue.text: Inspire people who dowse, say

definitions.note: a relative phrase standing for those who douse flames, an example signalled by say

parts.note: to fire someone is to inspire or rouse them
men are people

explanation.surface: A leader encourages water diviners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dowse' suggests water divining; here it is a spelling of douse, to drench a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigade crews put out blazes by drenching them with water.

clue.text: Man said to practise for carrying out post

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a vehicle that carries letters

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard, not written

parts.note: a man is male
to train is to practise

explanation.surface: A man is told to rehearse for taking a job abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job; it is the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway service dedicated to conveying letters and parcels.

clue.text: Mushroom exploded, losing top

indicators.note: losing means the following word is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: blew its top is an idiom for lost one's temper, exploded in anger

explanation.surface: A fungus bursts apart and loses its cap.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for losing one's temper loses its last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Blewits is an edible fungus with a lilac stem.

clue.text: Coal will eventually catch fire

indicators.note: eventually points to the end, so take the last letter of will

parts.note: to ignite is to catch fire

explanation.surface: Coal will eventually burst into flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Lignite is a soft brown variety of fuel dug from the ground, between peat and bituminous.

clue.text: Boy achieves century

parts.note: wins means achieves or gains
a ton is a hundred, as a century in cricket

explanation.surface: A lad scores a hundred runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston is a boy's name.

clue.text: Note wound in examination

parts.note: te is a note in tonic sol-fa
a sting is a wound from an insect

explanation.surface: A doctor makes a note of an injury during a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' is a noun, not the past of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing is the act of trying something out, an examination.

clue.text: One's drawn by advertisement

explanation.surface: A drawing is accompanied by a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled container is pulled along behind a car; a film preview promotes a forthcoming release.

clue.text: One up for musical prince

parts.note: someone up at university, as in the title role of a Romberg operetta about a royal heir at Heidelberg

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers for the role of a royal in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means in residence at university; The Student Prince is an operetta by Sigmund Romberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is up at university is enrolled there for study.

clue.text: Gone out to see off Italian

indicators.note: out means disordered, so these letters are rearranged
off means awry, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: Someone has left to wave off an Italian friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GONE to GENO; 'off' rearranges SEE to ESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Genoa, a port city in north-west Italy.

clue.text: Left to fetch explorer that's lost

parts.note: gone means left or departed
to go for something is to fetch it
a Burton, meaning an explorer like Sir Richard Burton

explanation.surface: Someone went off to find an explorer who had gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British RAF slang from the Second World War for killed or missing, now meaning ruined or lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has been destroyed or gone missing, in British slang.

clue.text: Special fare for conference

explanation.surface: A particular menu is served for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime of food followed for health; a formal assembly, as in the Diet of Worms.

clue.text: Spurious praise captivates better half

indicators.note: captivates means holds captive, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: adulate means to praise excessively

indicators.note: half takes the last three of the six letters of better

explanation.surface: Insincere flattery wins over one's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better half' looks like a spouse, but 'half' takes the back half of 'better', and 'captivates' encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, adulterate means debased or impure, thus not genuine.

clue.text: Brezhnev was a streaker

explanation.surface: The Soviet leader is said to have run naked.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of Soviet leader Brezhnev; also a meteor of the November shower, which streaks across the sky.

clue.text: Revelation of secret on news-stands, in print

indicators.note: a revelation exposes what was concealed, so letters within the words are exposed

explanation.surface: A secret is exposed on newspaper stands, appearing in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'print' looks like the press, but it is printed fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretonne is a heavy cotton fabric typically printed with patterns.
